author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
reference: Rule-set corpus for the Technical Requisition Builder, written from the public spec SPEC-technicalrequisition.md (state model 3, derived sets 4, rule table 5.2 with severity per issue purpose, verdict and ladder 6, register item 7.4, presets 9, corpus interface 13) and the standards the rules cite. It restates the five presets, then gives every one of the 66 rule ids a triggering case and a near-miss (the complete preset P1 at enquiry is the common near-miss for every rule it does not fire, as spec 9.1 states), probes the boundaries listed in spec 13.3 (FAT/SAT stage ranks, equal/one-day date comparisons, maturity order/enquiry/unrecognised, norm equality of keys and revisions, obligation from field vs shall/must/should/none, system vs package tagging, loaded:false per section, id collisions and unseen register revisions, flags on referenced, unreferenced and orphan targets), and checks derived ids, coverage fractions, VDRL stage counts, day windows, write refusal and register-item fields. Expected values come from hand-stated rule outcomes that an own stdlib Python engine (technicalrequisition-ref.py, written from the spec) must reproduce before the corpus is written; day windows use datetime.date differences.
reference_citations: ISO 9001:2015 clause 8.4.3 'Information for external providers' - opening sentence ('The organization shall ensure the adequacy of requirements prior to their communication to the external provider') and items 1-6 (a-f), wording checked 2026-09-22 against the reproduction at https://preteshbiswas.com/2023/09/05/iso-90012015-clause-8-4-3-information-for-external-providers/ (ISO text itself not opened); basis of TEC-R-001/020/030/039/050/060/062/063

IOGP S-723Q 'Quality Requirements for Electric Process Heaters', December 2020, https://jip33.iogp.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Quality-Reqs-Electric-Prcocess-Heaters-S-723Qv2020-12.pdf - clause 3.3 hold point ('... shall not proceed without the approval of the purchaser or purchaser's representative'), 3.4 witness point ('... the supplier shall notify the purchaser ... before proceeding'), 3.5 surveillance, 3.6 review; Annex A codes H, W, S, R (read 2026-09-22); basis of TEC-R-060/061/065

ISO 10845-1:2020 'Construction procurement - Part 1: Processes, methods and procedures', edition 2, December 2020, https://www.iso.org/standard/72467.html - title, edition and scope confirmed 2026-09-22 (public/private procurement-system standard); the clause titles 6.2.4/6.2.6/6.2.7 cited by the spec were not re-read here and no case depends on them

ISO/IEC Directives Part 2, 9th edition (2021), clause 7.2 Table 3 ('shall' = requirement) and 7.3 Table 4 ('should' = recommendation), as cited by the spec for the verbal-form obligation derivation; 'must' -> mandatory is the spec author's method

IOGP JIP33 information requirements form S-723L (December 2020) columns 'Submit With Proposal' / 'First Issue Post Purchase Order' / 'Required As Built' and purposes 'For Information' / 'For Acceptance', as cited by the spec for vocabularies 3.3 A and E (not re-read here; no case depends on the source wording)
PIP (Process Industry Practices): no requisition template verified; nothing cited
tolerance: exact for every check: the model has no continuous quantity. Verdicts are categorical; counts, coverage fractions [k, n], stage counts and day windows are integers (spec 13.2), so any deviation is a logic difference. rules_present: each listed id has >= 1 finding; rules_absent: each listed id has 0 findings; findings: set equality on the listed rules with multiplicity per spec 5.3, where 'target' is the offending list-item id (SC-/EX-/TP-/VDR-/ITP-), requirement or datasheet id, or register id (VD-), or for TEC-R-021 the list of ids carrying the key - a tool that prints a field path such as vdrl[VDR-03].due_stage matches when the path names that id. register_item compares only the listed fields; list elements compare only the listed keys, in order. No check is marked disputable: the eleven that were are resolved by the adjudications of 2026-09-23, which wrote each reading into the spec and left every reference unchanged. Numeric tolerances: none chosen; day windows are exact integer differences of UTC calendar dates.
not_benchmarked: Printed requisition layout, wording and the seven-language strings (presentation; browser and localisation QA)
Pull actions of spec 7.1 (which lines 'Add mandatory requirements', 'Attach package datasheets', 'Add expected vendor documents' insert): UI convenience over the same sets the rules define

Package transport: explicit load, ignored-section and ignored-field reporting, byte-identical write-back, package_revision drift confirmation, storage failure (package cases of TZ-project-package 7, structural checks)
Finding 'detail' texts (e.g. TEC-R-026 with/without counts, TEC-R-044 key lists) beyond the rule id, severity and target
Permalink size limit (4 kB) and context omission, record() contents other than the empty-state null
Input-form validation of out-of-list enum values (stored as '' per spec 3.1): the corpus supplies in-vocabulary enums only
The VDRL due-stage ladder figure (acceptance criterion 15)
Technical adequacy of requirements, datasheet values or tests (outside the model, spec 2)
coverage: All 66 rule ids of spec 5.4: each has at least one triggering case and at least one case where it is asserted absent (P1 at enquiry for every rule except 026/038/044, plus targeted near-misses at the stated boundaries). Headline claims of the owner brief: omitted tagged mandatory requirement (030), datasheet not at latest revision / not attached (040/041), below-order maturity blocks purchase but not enquiry (044), FAT-needed document due after FAT (051), exclusion contradicting scope (021), hold point without owner (060), revision history and issue purpose (005-011), purpose ladder. Boundaries of spec 13.3 all probed. Derived quantities: derived_id (slug, null, non-Latin, 60-char cut), mandatory_coverage, ds_coverage, params_below_order, vdrl_by_stage, clarification/bid windows including a leap-year span, write refusal (001/003/090/091 and 'blocked but writable'), register item fields, empty state. Added by adjudication 2026-09-23 (six cases, references computed independently from the spec by a third implementation of sections 3-7): TEC-R-090 on requirement_id and datasheet_id, the two lists spec 3.4 names that no earlier case duplicated; TEC-R-021 multiplicity with two contradicting keys, one of them carried by three scope rows; TEC-R-006 multiplicity with two distinct repeated revision values; spec 6's rule that a 'blocked' verdict outside {001, 003, 090, 091} still permits the register write; TEC-R-095 firing while the requirements register is unloaded against TEC-R-097 staying silent there (spec 5.2 needs column); and the TEC-R-098 detail carrying TEC-R-030 when that rule's state condition, not a loaded flag, is what suppressed it. Added 2026-09-23 after the spec fixed §5.3 and §3.3 B: one case attaches DS-p-101 twice at two revisions, pinning TEC-R-044/045 to one finding per register datasheet id (and §4.3 to 2 of 3 parameters counted once) while TEC-R-041 stays one finding per attached line; the 'ORDER' maturity case is no longer marked disputable, since the five spellings are now matched byte for byte. Added by adjudication 2026-09-23 (second round, twelve cases, every reference computed from the spec by a third implementation of sections 3-7 and not copied from the tool): TEC-R-052 at as_built with all three ladder rows graded, the SAT twin of TEC-R-051 whose purchase-column blocker no earlier case pinned; one state firing all nine rules whose severity rises with the issue purpose (022, 023, 030, 035, 040, 041, 050, 054, 095) with all three ladder rows graded; spec 4.3 with equipment_datasheets unloaded while the snapshot still holds entries; TEC-R-090 against blank ids; ds_coverage with one datasheet attached twice at the current revision against the parameter count keyed on the datasheet id; derived_id at a 60-character slug with no trailing dash to trim; a blank package_id against a register whose rows are blank too; and five cases whose ids, item key, maturity and flag target are spelled like properties of the host language's base object (constructor, toString, valueOf), which spec 3.4 now says are ordinary strings. A thirteenth case pins TEC-R-092 against a register revision spelled 'constructor', the direction in which that defect class hides a finding instead of inventing one.

Spec 3.4: no spelling is special, and a revision whose text happens to name a property of the host language's base object is compared like any other string.
